cases.why: FOUR FIELDS. No lane, no score, no flags, no HMAC, no object key, no history — that is the whole body. `revision` (D8) is the number this service assigned to the bytes it stored.

THE FORGERY-TUNING ORACLE, pinned as a fixture. A forensics score handed to the person who uploaded the file lets them edit, re-upload and watch the number move until GREEN. Do not build an applicant-facing document-quality indicator; no endpoint will ever feed it.
The storage key is derived from closed-set inputs and never returned. Handing it to a browser is a read primitive into the object store.
The client's filename is validated and then IGNORED. Do not expect it back.

THE ONE EXCEPTION to withholding verdicts. A binary antivirus result teaches a forger nothing, and silently accepting an infected file the citizen believes was received is unusable for a legal process.
Carries what the client CLAIMED. The sniffed type is deliberately not returned — that would be a hint about the detector.
Not legal for the OWNING agency, derived from ownership and never from the request. Drive the upload UI from AGENCY_DOCUMENT_TYPES or the citizen gets a 422 they cannot act on.
Even the refusal must not carry a lane.
The officer-grade verdict. Legitimate here because the caller is a service, not the document's author — but never proxy this response to a browser.
RECORDED DEFECT: this controller keys BUSINESS OUTCOMES on error, unique among the platform's fifteen controllers. A client here cannot tell a business outcome from a transport fault.
The record exists; its bytes do not.
Pins the defect in place so re-keying it to status is a deliberate, visible change rather than a silent one.
409 with currentStatus — the status IS the explanation.
objectBucket is optional and defaults to usrp-documents.
This route takes a REFERENCE, not bytes. Bytes go to the multipart upload route.
The file part MUST be named exactly 'file'. A differently named part is 400 MISSING_FILE, not a warning.
Four parts, correctly named.

D8 (verified at backend 4683b5615daeecdf13b40bb4930c3aeec83196de, the merge of e-recruitment PR #61). A 201 with no `revision` is not this contract. A caller that treats it as success has to invent the number, and an invented revision on an evidence screen is worse than a refused read.
Revisions start at 1. Zero is not a revision; it is the absence of one with a type attached.
A revision is a whole count of accepted uploads in a slot. 2.5 is contract drift, and printing it as a revision invents evidence.
A stringified number is how a revision arrives when a row was JSON-stringified. It must be refused, not coerced: coercion is how "2" becomes a revision nobody assigned.
Past the safe-integer range a number is no longer a countable revision: it silently equals its neighbours. The gateway applies the same rule (Number.isSafeInteger).
D8. An officer has reviewed this document. Nothing was written: the refusal is decided before the object write, inside the slot lock.
D8. The application has moved past document review. Same status, different ground: the citizen must be told the two things differently.
A reason outside the closed set is drift, not copy. A client must fall back to a generic message rather than print a string an upstream added last night.
Without a reason the refusal cannot be explained, and a bare code printed as copy leaks an internal vocabulary to a citizen.
The union's first member: the application is not collecting documents, and the currentStatus is the explanation.
The union's D8 member: same status, different ground. A client MUST discriminate on `error`, not on the status code, or it will show a citizen the wrong sentence.
A third code on this status is not this contract.
